QF.id: AIFM CIII Legal Documents and Negotiations_1

question.text: Himalaya Arbitrage Fund, a Cat III AIF, is being constituted as a trust. Which of the following statements about the Trust Indenture is CORRECT from the legal-documentation perspective?

answer.text: The Trust Indenture can remain unregistered provided SEBI has registered the AIF under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012.
The Trust Indenture is a registered document executed between the Trust Settlor and the Trustee and brings the trust into existence.
The Trust Indenture is signed only by the Investment Manager and the Sponsor; the Trustee is a mere observer.
The Trust Indenture is optional when the AIF uses a unified master-feeder structure at GIFT-IFSC.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 9.2, when an AIF is constituted as a trust, the Trust Indenture is a REGISTERED document executed between the Trust Settlor and the Trustee that brings the trust into existence; AIF Regulations further mandate its registration. The trust itself has no separate legal personality, so this registered indenture is legally essential. The Trap: Option A confuses SEBI AIF registration with Indian Trusts Act registration — they are distinct and BOTH are required. Option C wrongly drops the Trustee, who is in fact the counter-party to the Settlor. Option D invents an IFSC carve-out that the chapter does not recognize. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C (All-Cat Manager) tests the same constitutional-document concept for both PE/VC and hedge-fund tracks. XIX-D (Cat I/II Manager) emphasizes Trust Indenture in the drawdown-fund context. XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) only tests the name. Manager's Pro-Tip: On a Cat III hedge-fund desk, check that the Trust Indenture pre-dates the first PMS-style subscription and that Clause on 'determinate trust' status is airtight — tax officials rely on it to treat gains at fund level MMR without disputing corpus beneficiaries.
